findings.description: The RDS instance sets storage_encrypted = false, so the database volume, snapshots and backing storage hold data in cleartext with no KMS protection.

publicly_accessible = true assigns the MySQL instance a public endpoint reachable from the internet, exposing the database to internet-based credential attacks and exploitation of MySQL vulnerabilities.

The master username is the predictable default 'admin' and the password is supplied via a plain Terraform variable rather than Secrets Manager/KMS, so it will be stored in cleartext in the state file and CI logs.
iam_database_authentication_enabled is not set, so authentication relies solely on the static master password with no centrally-managed, short-lived IAM token option.

No enabled_cloudwatch_logs_exports (audit/error/general/slowquery) are configured, leaving no record of database authentication or query activity for detecting compromise of a publicly-reachable database.

The MySQL parameter group does not set require_secure_transport = ON (nor is any TLS enforcement configured on the instance), so clients — including the app server — may connect to the internet-exposed database over unencrypted connections.

The inline role policy grants s3:*, ec2:* and rds:* on Resource "*". This role is attached to the internet-facing db_app EC2 instance, so any compromise of the web application yields full control of all S3 data, EC2 (including instance/role manipulation for privilege escalation) and RDS in the account.

The user_data script interpolates the RDS master username and var.password into a PHP include file. EC2 user data is retrievable in cleartext via the instance metadata service and stored in Terraform state, so any SSRF or local access on the host leaks the database master password.

No metadata_options block requiring http_tokens = "required" is set, so IMDSv1 remains enabled; a single SSRF in the PHP application would expose the instance profile credentials for the wildcard s3/ec2/rds role and the plaintext user-data secrets.
No root_block_device or ebs_block_device encryption is configured, so the instance volume — which contains the DB credentials written to /var/www/inc/dbinfo.inc — may be stored unencrypted.
The database security group permits all protocols and ports outbound to 0.0.0.0/0, providing an unrestricted data-exfiltration and command-and-control path from the database tier.

The RDS security group is paired with a publicly_accessible instance; combined with the wide-open egress rule and no description or explicit deny boundary, the database tier lacks meaningful network segmentation from the internet.
